feedback.problem:
Consider the line $x=1$ and linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

What is the equation of the image of the line under the action of $T?$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, notice that the line $x=1$ passes through the points $J(1,0)$ and $K(1,1)$ since the coordinates of both points satisfy the equation.

To find the image of $J$ and $K$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing the coordinates of the points:

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective image points are ${J}^{′}(2,1)$ and ${K}^{′}(0,4).$

Finally, we write the equation of the line that passes through ${J}^{′}$ and ${K}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}}(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-1 & =\frac{4-1}{0-2}(x-2) \\ y-1 & =-\frac{3}{2}(x-2) \\ 2y-2 & =-3x+6 \\ 3x+2y-8 & =0\end{aligned}
$$
